transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start time: 10:30 AM UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen, Arjun Patel, Lena Morales, Daniel Park, Maya Lopez, Hugo Kim, Priya Desai, Marcus Reynolds

Summary: Quick sync to align product + eng on Q4 launches, go/no-go criteria for Dedicated/Private features, and review of the 09-10 outage. Not a customer call - internal planning.

[00:00] Sofia: okay everyone thanks for joining, I'm gonna kick off, short agenda - roadmap, launch readiness checklist, and then the incident followup from last week. we got 75 minutes, but i wanna keep it tight.
[00:28] Arjun: sounds good, quick heads up we already started the load tests on the qps patterns Hugo shipped over, saw some tail latency at higher concurrencies, so that's gonna factor into the rollout thresholds.
[00:45] Hugo: yeah, those were the 95/99 numbers, i think the 99.9 is still noisy cause of the small sample, but it's real.
[01:15] Lena: and from SRE side the 09-10 partial outage - root cause looks like a KV cache eviction spike combined with a bad autoscaler bump. we have the initial logs but still reconciling traces.
[01:47] Maya: can we get a tl;dr on the impact? what customers were affected?
[02:05] Marcus: Support saw approx 12 tenants with degraded responses for ~6-8 minutes, no data loss but some requests timed out and retried, higher costs for retries.
[02:30] Sofia: okay, so the three things i want for launch readiness: runbook updated, canary rollout plan with thresholds, and a final regression signoff. who wants to own each?
[02:55] Arjun: i'll own the canary rollout doc, i'll include traffic shaping params and rollback criteria.
[03:10] Priya: QA will do the regression and smoke tests, i'll schedule test window with infra.
[03:25] Lena: SRE will update the on-call runbook and add specific KV cache mitigations plus autoscaler guardrails.
[03:45] Daniel: Product ops - i'll coordinate communication and the benchmark spreadsheet to include cost deltas.
[04:10] Sofia: awesome. next, roadmap: we have limited slots for Q4, need to prioritize Dedicated performance optimizations, Private deployment security hardening, and the billing/usage analytics feature. Thoughts?
[04:36] Arjun: from infra perspective, the performance optimizations (kernel selection & batching improvements) give biggest impact on cost per token, but need ~6 weeks of eng time to stabilize.
[04:55] Hugo: also the KV cache improvements will reduce tail latency which hits P99. it's more of an engineering lift but high value.
[05:20] Maya: product-wise customers care most about predictable latency and security controls, so Private features and SSO/KMS work should be high priority.
[05:45] Sofia: ok let's triage: top priority - KV cache stabilization + autoscaler guardrails; second - Dedicated batching & kernel selection; third - Private security hardening and billing UX. we'll put this in the board.
[06:10] [Brief side conversation - crosstalk] Hugo: sorry, just a quick note, the benchmark we ran used the v2 model shim, not v3, that might skew numbers.
[06:30] Arjun: good catch, we should re-run with v3 and the longer sequence lengths we expect in production. Daniel - can you add that to benchmarks?
[06:48] Daniel: on it, i'll add v3 and seq len 1024 runs.
[07:05] Sofia: incident deep dive - Lena, take us through the timeline from 09-10.
[07:22] Lena: timeline: 02:12 UTC we saw increased request queueing, 02:14 autoscaler triggered extra pods, 02:15 eviction pressure in KV caused evictions, 02:18 a subset of requests hit cache-miss storms and we saw timeouts. by 02:20 the system recovered after manual throttle.
[07:50] Hannah: (note - not present)
[08:05] Hugo: the eviction thresholds were misaligned with recent memory growth from a model update, looks like a tuned threshold needs to be higher for the new model sizes.
[08:30] Lena: yes, and autoscaler policy didn't include the kv-eviction signal so it scaled in a way that exacerbated the issue.
[08:50] Arjun: so root causes: model memory growth + kv-eviction mis-tuned thresholds + autoscaler policy gaps. We need immediate mitigations and a longer term plan.
[09:10] Sofia: what's the immediate mitigation?
[09:25] Lena: short-term: increase eviction threshold on the hot path, add a temporary autoscaler cooldown and make the autoscaler check kv metrics before scaling decisions.
[09:45] Priya: QA, will we need to re-run anything to validate the mitigation?
[09:58] Lena: yes we'll run a smoke on the cache eviction scenario and watch tail latencies. Priya please coordinate.
[10:20] [00:10:20] Daniel: on the longer term, we should add a KV cache pressure metric to the alerting dashboard and a specific incident playbook entry.
[10:40] Arjun: also, adding a fallback model variant for low memory mode could reduce memory footprint during spikes. that's more work but might pay off.
[11:05] Sofia: ok can we agree owners? Lena - runbook + metrics, Arjun - fallback variant feasibility, Priya - test validation, Daniel - benchmark + cost impact, Sofia - prioritize and publish roadmap.
[11:30] All: agreed.
[12:00] [~12:00] Sofia: Launch gating criteria we want: P99 latency under X ms at target load, no critical alerts for 48 hours in canary, cost delta within budget threshold. we'll define exact numbers in the rollout doc.
[12:30] Arjun: propose P99 <= 420ms at target load, and canary for 24 hours with a 5% traffic ramp if we hit 48-hour regression we hold.
[13:05] Hugo: the 420ms might be tight for some workloads, maybe allow a tiered SLA - Bronze/Silver/Gold.
[13:22] Sofia: we'll add tiering to the product doc but for initial launch let's shoot for the middle ground.
[13:42] [Short pause - note taking]
[14:15] Daniel: on benchmarking, i'll share a spreadsheet with cost per million tokens delta between current and optimized runs, include v3 numbers and sequence len 1024.
[14:40] Priya: QA asks for a regression matrix - i'll add perf tests + integration + security smoke.
[15:05] Sofia: great. timeline recap: Sofia publishes prioritized tickets by 09-17, Lena draft runbook by 09-18, Arjun rollout doc by 09-20, Daniel benchmark by 09-21, Priya regression schedule by 09-22.
[15:30] Hugo: quick note - we also discussed encryption/KMS changes for Private; that has compliance implications and might need security signoff.
[15:50] Arjun: we should loop in Security for the KMS plan, will do after we finalize the design.
[16:12] Sofia: any blockers we're aware of?
[16:30] Priya: dependency on infra to run full-scale tests, need staging capacity increase.
[16:45] Daniel: cost for extra staging infra - will raise in ops.
[17:05] Lena: on-call bandwidth next week limited due to conferences; will note it in schedule.
[17:30] Sofia: ok last bit - communication, who drafts the launch announcement and customer-facing docs?
[17:45] Daniel: product ops will draft, marketing will review, and support will get the FAQ.
[18:05] Sofia: perfect. quick recap of action items, owners and due dates - we'll post into the shared channel. thanks everyone.
[18:30] [End of recorded portion - remaining discussion was scheduling and small clarifications not captured in detail]
